ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  MEETING NOTES
  November 6, 2017

1. CALL TO ORDER

  CHAIRWOMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2. ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Mitchell, Krieger, Larson, Radocchio, Vona

  Committee Members Absent:  Warner, Giglia, Chan-Southwell, Stegura

  Staff Members Present:  Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager
  Jeannie Naughton, Sr. Planner

  There being no quorum, the EAC proceeded with an informal discussion. As such, the
  following are notes for informational purposes only. No action was taken.

3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A. ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF JULY 31, 2017.

  There being no quorum, no action could be taken.

4. AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  None

5. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  CLIMATE ACTION PLAN – PHASE II

  Staff Member Davis summarized the staff report on the City of Rolling Hills Estates’ Climate
  Action Plan and stated that this discussion will focus on Phase II of the Climate Action Plan.
  Phase I was establishing baseline targets and creating an inventory of carbon emmissions.
  In 2015 Council adopted Phase I, which included the baseline targets plus an energy
  efficiency chapter. Phase II outlines land use, transportation, greening, energy storage, and
  generation measures. It is a visioning document which will help facilitate policy.

  Kim Fuentes, Deputy Executive Director, South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG)
  added that the Climate Action Plan also helps Cities secure funding. Ms. Fuentes provided a
  presentation on the Climate Action Plan.

Environmental Advisory Committee
Meeting Notes, November 6, 2017
  1
   In response to a question by CHAIR MITCHELL, Ms. Fuentes stated that the goals for the
  City are in line with the goals of the State.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO, Ms. Fuentes stated that
  when residents are using a lot of water, there is a relationship between the usage and the
  energy used to move the water.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER KREIGER, Ms. Fuentes stated that the
  data is collected from a number of sources, some which include utility company and state data.

  Ms. Fuentes added that the City is doing well according to State measures and if the City
  stays on track with goals, the goals set for 2035 will be achieved.

  The chapters of the Climate Action Plan, include, Energy Efficiency, Solid Waste, Urban
  Greening, Energy Generation and Storage, and Land Use and Transportation.

  In regards to the Land Use and Transportation (LUT) section on the graph, which shows
  possible reductions in GHGs, Sr. Planner Naughton stated that a lot of the measures in LUT
  are items that will be explored during the General Plan Update. Therefore, there is not enough
  quantifiable data to input into the modeling to provide a true representation of what the City’s
  gain could be, if all measures were implemented.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER KRIEGER, Staff Member Davis stated
  that there will be an item at the City Council meeting of November 14th, in regards to the
  contract with waste management and there is a proposed change to the calculation of manure
  waste pick-up.

  Aaron Baum, SBCCOG, stated that there will be opportunities for more programs.

  In regards to urban greening, COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO expressed his concern
  with more water usage green open space is increased. In addition, he asked about the City’s
  policy on replacing trees that have been removed by the City.

  In regards to land use and transportation, COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO asked if
  transportation by bicycle is a viable option. CHAIR MITCHELL stated that although there are
  bicyclists who ride in the City as a sport or exercise, however, as transportation it would be
  difficult due to all of the hills throughout the City. Batter powered bikes have been discussed
  as an alternative. Ms. Fuentes stated that transportation by bicycle may work in some
  sections of the City.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO, Staff Member
  Naughton stated that currently there are no affordable housing developments in the City.

  Ms. Fuentes and Members of the EAC concluded the meeting. Due to the lack of a
  quorum, no action was taken on this item.
